topic.name: Combining the Rules of Exponents With Algebraic Expressions

question.explanation:
We start by using the power of quotient rule: \begin{align*} \left(\dfrac {3y} {x^2}\right)^3 &=\\[3pt] \dfrac {(3y)^3} {\left(x^2\right)^3} & \end{align*}

Then, we apply the power of product rule in the numerator and the power rule in the denominator: \begin{align*} \dfrac {(3y)^3} {\left(x^2\right)^3} &=\\[3pt] \dfrac {3^3y^3} {x^{2 \cdot 3}} &=\\[3pt] \dfrac {27y^3} {x^6}& \end{align*}

example.title: Combining the Rules of Exponents With Fractions

question.explanation:
First, we substitute for $x$ and $y\mathbin{:}$ \[ \eqalign{ xy&= \left(\dfrac{81a^8}{b^2c^3}\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{b^7c^{11}}{9a^4}\right) \\[3pt] &= \dfrac{81a^8b^7c^{11}}{9a^4b^2c^3} } \]

Then, we separate the fraction, group the three variables separately, and apply the quotient rule: \[ \eqalign{ \dfrac{81a^8b^7c^{11}}{9a^4b^2c^3}&=\\[3pt] \dfrac{81}{9} \cdot \dfrac{a^8}{a^4} \cdot \dfrac{b^7}{b^2} \cdot \dfrac{c^{11}}{c^3} &=\\[3pt] \dfrac{81}{9}\cdot a^{(8-4)}\cdot b^{(7-2)}\cdot c^{(11-3)}&=\\[3pt] 9a^4b^5c^8 & } \]

example.title: Combining the Rules of Exponents With Fractions

question.explanation:
We start by using the product rule in the numerator: \begin{align} \dfrac{y^2\cdot y^{13}}{y^{12}} &=y^{n}\\[3pt] \dfrac{y^{2+13}}{y^{12}} &=y^{n}\\[3pt] \dfrac{y^{15}}{y^{12}}&= y^{n} \end{align} Then, we apply the quotient rule: \begin{align*} \dfrac{y^{15}}{y^{12}}&= y^n\\[3pt] y^{15+(-12)} &= y^n\\[3pt] y^3 &= y^n \end{align*}

Finally, since both sides of the equation share the same base ($y$), we can equate the exponents: \begin{align} y^3 &=y^{n} \\[3pt] 3 &= n \end{align}

Hence, $n=3.$
